item.title: “It’s getting harder and harder to be at Wellesley”: When financial aid falls short
item.description: Iris Zhan and Lauren Venturella contributed to interviews and data collection. Her cost of attendance came out to be nearly three times the $450 she was expected to pay her first semester at Wellesley — totaling $1,300. Jaiyeola, who...

item.title: To speak or not to speak: A closer look at the ICE OUT rally
item.description: Snowflakes whipped against my face in the sharp wind as my friend and I stepped out of the Copley Square subway station. I pulled my coat tighter, navigating a path of slush and half-melted ice. Despite temperatures dropping below 10°F, thousands braved the freeze, filling the space around the Boston Public Library. item.title: Editor’s Corner: On Wellesley’s mAIrtyrdom
item.description: AI is a scary word for many of us here at Wellesley. For obvious reasons, instructors have added a no-AI clause to their syllabi, and students are reducing their use of em dashes and ignoring Grammarly’s suggestions to avoid false accusations. item.title: 2000 Meters to Andriivka: Insight into War
item.description: The Temerty Contemporary Ukraine Program (TCUP) at Harvard University Ukrainian Research Institute hosted its annual conference in late January.

item.title: Heaven is a place at Wellesley with “Head Over Heels”
item.description: This past weekend, the lights of the Ruth Nagel Jones Black Box Theater shone brightly on a giant pride flag painted on the stage. The occasion was Wellesley Upstage’s production of “Head Over Heels,” a jukebox musical featuring the music of the Go-Go’s directed by Taryn Castro.

item.title: Rose Windows and Royal Crypts OR In defense of the Parisian Cathédrale
item.description: This Wintersession, I traveled to Paris, France, with the Wellesley College French and Francophone Studies Department… I soon discovered one of the best-kept secrets of the city: it is teeming with breathtaking churches.

item.title: No Other Choice for employment? Watch this movie
item.description: This review is dedicated to all the sibs who are struggling to find internships and jobs. Please remember you have Other Choices. Good luck!

item.title: Concert Review: Daffo at the Middle East Club
item.description: Those fortunate enough to be chosen by the algorithm have a chance to turn brief visibility into something more tangible. Judging by the warmth at their Cambridge show, it is clear that Daffo is on that route.
